clue.text: Stop in cobbled side street

indicators.note: something cobbled together is roughly assembled, so the letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
ST is the usual abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Someone halts in a narrow cobblestone lane off the main road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobbled' looks like it describes the street's paving, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or leave off doing something, a formal synonym for halting.

clue.text: Set down almost half a dozen in storehouse

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a depot is a warehouse or store

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: half a dozen is six

explanation.surface: An instruction to put six items into a warehouse, give or take one.
explanation.walkthrough: Half a dozen is a roundabout way to say a number; trimming it leaves a two-letter piece that slots inside the storehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is something laid down, and to deposit is to place or put something in position.

clue.text: Vase held by sculpted saint seen on top of Elgar's grave

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it, so the vessel sits within the reworked letters
sculpting reshapes material, so the letters of the word are remodelled

parts.note: taken as written
an urn is a vase, often for ashes

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A funeral urn and a carved saint stand on a composer's tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' reads as the burial place, but it is the adjective meaning solemn. The rearranged saint wraps around the urn, and Elgar's first letter follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a gloomy, sombre, serious temperament, the same mood as grave in its adjectival sense.

clue.text: Outline of small boat

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A rough drawing showing the shape of a little sailing vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the silhouette of a little vessel, but 'Outline' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing or brief summary giving only the main lines of something.

clue.text: Indifferent about protecting extremely inflamed blister near the mouth

parts.note: a cold response is an uninterested, unfeeling one
so means very, as in so tired
re is the Latin-derived word for concerning

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a painful mouth blister with indifference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Protecting' is loose here: the word for extremely stands guard in front of the word for about, rather than around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold sore is a herpes lesion that erupts as a painful inflamed spot on or around the lips.

clue.text: An honour to accept Orbison's first instrument

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece is received inside the other

parts.note: the OBE is a British order awarded as an honour

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the following word only

parts.note: the opening letter of the singer's name

explanation.surface: Roy Orbison is offered a royal award for his first instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Break off to criticise girl in front of Rex

parts.note: diss is slang for disparage
a girl's name
R is the abbreviation for Rex, king

explanation.surface: A girl is criticised for standing ahead of a king, or a man named Rex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In front of' just places EVE before R.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissever is to sever or split apart, an old-fashioned word for separating forcibly.

clue.text: Rowe oddly neglected to include talk about language

indicators.note: including something means holding it inside, so one piece wraps the other
neglecting the odd positions keeps only the second and fourth letters

parts.note: the even letters remain once the odd ones are dropped

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: gas is idle chatter

explanation.surface: Someone called Rowe has, strangely, failed to bring up a topic of discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Osage is the Siouan tongue of the Osage people of Oklahoma, a Native American language.

clue.text: Implore conservationists to step in before soldiers return

indicators.note: stepping in means entering, so the group goes inside the word that follows

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
the National Trust conserves historic British properties

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone begs environmentalists to intervene before troops come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' looks like it only orders the pieces, but it is a poetic synonym that holds the conservationists.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to ask earnestly or plead, the same as begging or imploring.

clue.text: Make publicly known at opening of parish club

indicators.note: the opening of a word is where it begins, its first letter

parts.note: the initial letter
to utter is to give voice to or circulate

explanation.surface: An announcement made at the opening of a parish social club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a society, but it is a golf club. UTTER follows the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A putter is the golf club used on the green to roll the ball towards the hole.

clue.text: Carefully studies article going into race being fixed

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: going into something means entering it, so the small word sits inside the race

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A punter pores over a newspaper story about a race that has been rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixed' suggests a crooked race, but it means unchanging.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constant stays the same and does not vary, which is one sense of being set or steady.

clue.text: Significant to find Swiss nationalist in government

parts.note: William Tell, legendary hero of Swiss independence
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A noteworthy discovery: a Swiss patriot sitting in government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a position, but it supplies its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling detail is revealing or striking, carrying weight and meaning.

clue.text: Seriously affected by changes to trek in South Carolina

indicators.note: changes made to something alter its form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
SC is the state abbreviation

explanation.surface: Travellers in South Carolina are badly hit by alterations to their journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stricken is to be gravely hit or afflicted, by illness or misfortune for example.

clue.text: Unruffled by prophet in conversation about space

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the sound-alike wraps round the next piece
in conversation means spoken, so what counts is how the word sounds

parts.note: a seer foretells the future
an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm while a prophet chats about outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a typesetting space, half an em, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A serene person is calm and untroubled, smooth like water that nothing disturbs.

clue.text: Run for a time with a couple of teachers after work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: a couple means two, so just the first two letters are kept

parts.note: the opening two letters

explanation.surface: Someone runs a business for a spell, with two teachers helping once work is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After work' places the other pieces after the musical work's abbreviation; 'for' merely joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to manage or work a business or machine, which is what running it means.

clue.text: Struggle over stopping it turning left

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way, so the word runs backwards
stopping a gap plugs it, so one piece fills the middle of the other

parts.note: taken as written
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A driver fights to stop the car from turning left.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is turned round to TI, O plugs the gap inside it, and L ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To toil is to labour hard and wearily, which is struggling at a task.

clue.text: Key on laptop due to be replaced is of no more use

parts.note: C is a musical key

indicators.note: replacing means putting back differently, so the letters are set down in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A broken laptop key means the machine is useless and ought to be replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like a keyboard key, but it is a musical key. Clapped-out is British slang for worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: A clapped-out machine is worn out and broken down, past serving any purpose.

clue.text: Be born in spring

definitions.meaning: second meaning: arise or issue from a source

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' reads as the season of birth, but it is the verb meaning to arise.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin, arise, or come into being, so it fits both being born and springing up.

clue.text: Congregate in dining area in island retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the whole construction is read in reverse
being in a place means being inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile
a mess is where service personnel eat

explanation.surface: People gather in a canteen at an island hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The dining area goes inside Napoleon's island just before its final letter, and only then is the whole construction turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to gather together in one place, which is what a crowd does when it congregates.

clue.text: Old agricultural workers taking in Liberal leader's inconsequential remark

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing, so the larger word swallows the smaller piece

parts.note: the peasantry were the farm labourers of old

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its head

parts.note: its leading letter

explanation.surface: Old farmhands absorb a Liberal party chief's trivial comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal leader' suggests the head of the Liberal party, but just means the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a polite or joking remark of little weight, small talk exchanged for courtesy.

clue.text: Criticise American revolutionary's swagger

parts.note: to pan is to review harshly
A is the abbreviation for American
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: Someone attacks the American rebel's cocky strut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American revolutionary' looks like one person, a founding father, but splits into A and CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence of style, close to the self-assured flair of a swagger.

clue.text: Proceed with difficulty when airship fails to start

indicators.note: failing to start means missing the beginning, so the first letter is lost

parts.note: a blimp is a non-rigid airship

explanation.surface: An airship struggles along when its engine won't fire.
explanation.walkthrough: BLIMP loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To limp is to walk lamely or move along slowly and with effort, as a damaged vessel does.

clue.text: Speculation over general's tart

indicators.note: over means covering, so the bet spreads across the abbreviation on both sides

parts.note: a punt is a bet or gamble
GEN is the abbreviation for general

explanation.surface: Gossip about a general's mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' tempts as a noun, a pastry or a loose woman, but is the adjective meaning sharp. PUNT spreads over GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent taste is sharp and biting, like the sour sharpness described as tart.

clue.text: End of public holidays in Split

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter
leave is time off work

explanation.surface: Bank holidays finish in Split, the Croatian resort city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' with its capital letter looks like the Croatian city, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to cut or split apart, as with a cleaver.

clue.text: Not a hint of dyspepsia after she ate

parts.note: no as a negative
taken as written

indicators.note: a hint is the smallest trace, just the word's first letter

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: She ate a meal and suffered no indigestion afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After she' places the D after SHE. Nosh is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: To nosh is informal British for eating, so noshed means ate.

clue.text: Waller perhaps turned to Falkland initially for support

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the nickname runs backwards

parts.note: Fats Waller, the American jazz pianist

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the island group's name

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone named Waller looked to the Falklands for backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' says Waller is an example of a FATS: Fats Waller.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a stick or pole to lean on, so it is a physical prop.

clue.text: Horse around a lot in the middle of Oslo

indicators.note: horsing around is fooling about, so the letters are jumbled freely

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the middle of a four-letter word is its two central letters

parts.note: the two central letters

explanation.surface: A horse fools about a great deal in the centre of Norway's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse around' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'Horse' is the definition and 'around' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated adult male horse, kept for breeding.

clue.text: Acknowledge an American astronomer in speech

indicators.note: in speech means spoken, so the surname is matched by its sound

parts.note: George Ellery Hale, the American astronomer

explanation.surface: Recognising an American stargazer in a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail someone is to greet or salute them, a form of acknowledging their presence.

clue.text: Material to make underwear collected by girl after church

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church

indicators.note: collected by means gathered up by, so the girl holds the garment inside her

parts.note: a girl's name
a bra is an undergarment

explanation.surface: A girl after church picks up fabric to sew herself underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After church' places the girl, with her garment tucked inside, after the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambray is a light cotton fabric woven with coloured warp and white weft, so it is a cloth.

clue.text: Sack Virginia during a fit of madness

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the state sits inside the fit

parts.note: a rage is a violent outburst of anger
VA is the state abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone fires a woman named Virginia in a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' suggests dismissal from a job, but here it means plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder and lay waste to it, the same as ravaging it.

clue.text: Make weak literary tailor back off from scrap at first

indicators.note: with its back off a word loses its last letter

parts.note: an end is a leftover remnant, as in odds and ends
Francis Feeble, the woman's tailor in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2

explanation.surface: A tailor in a novel retreats from a fight before it starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a fight, but is a remnant: END loses its back letter and goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To enfeeble is to drain someone of strength, rendering them frail and debilitated.

clue.text: Union dispute ultimately leads to workers appearing in court

indicators.note: appearing in court means standing inside it, so the pieces go within

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
men as a workforce

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the last letter is used

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: A trade union's quarrel ends with staff summoned to a tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' looks like a trade union, but means a bond.
explanation.definitionFit: Cement is a binding substance or a uniting tie, so it is a bond that holds things together.
